prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: 2024年10月员工工资条 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 8 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes.
Merged cells: "姓名" spans 1 col × 2 row; "应发" spans 3 col × 1 row; "扣款" spans 3 col × 1 row; "实发" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Measured content facts (text px at 17px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "姓名" · longest unbreakable unit 18px · widest one-line content 53px
  col 2: header "应发 › 基本工资" · longest unbreakable unit 70px · widest one-line content 70px
  col 3: header "应发 › 绩效" · longest unbreakable unit 65px · widest one-line content 65px
  col 4: header "应发 › 补贴" · longest unbreakable unit 63px · widest one-line content 63px
  col 5: header "扣款 › 社保" · longest unbreakable unit 56px · widest one-line content 56px
  col 6: header "扣款 › 公积金" · longest unbreakable unit 63px · widest one-line content 63px
  col 7: header "扣款 › 个税" · longest unbreakable unit 60px · widest one-line content 60px
  col 8: header "实发" · longest unbreakable unit 71px · widest one-line content 71px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 601px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). The table, including its 1px outer border, must be at most 601px wide (column widths sum to at most 600px); no horizontal scrolling. A table exactly 601px wide fits.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Several designers worked independently on this table. You see their final layouts, anonymised as Layout P, Layout Q, Layout R, Layout S, Layout T, in that order after the overview: Layout P, Layout Q, Layout R, Layout S, Layout T.
Measured facts:
Layout P: column widths [74, 91, 86, 84, 55, 57, 60, 93] px · table 601×500 px · row heights [39, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66] · column headers on >1 line: 2/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 18 · fits the 601 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout Q: column widths [74, 91, 86, 63, 77, 57, 60, 92] px · table 601×500 px · row heights [39, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66] · column headers on >1 line: 1/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 18 · fits the 601 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout R: column widths [74, 72, 60, 60, 77, 84, 81, 92] px · table 601×500 px · row heights [39, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66] · column headers on >1 line: 1/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 18 · fits the 601 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout S: column widths [74, 91, 86, 84, 56, 57, 60, 92] px · table 601×500 px · row heights [39, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66] · column headers on >1 line: 1/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 18 · fits the 601 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout T: column widths [74, 91, 80, 75, 65, 65, 58, 92] px · table 601×500 px · row heights [39, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66] · column headers on >1 line: 1/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 30 · fits the 601 px viewport (no scrolling)

Compare them side by side. For each layout name its strengths, its faults and the spatial logic behind it (how it distributes space and why). Do not just pick a winner: you may combine the strengths of several layouts, propose something new, or overturn all of them. Propose up to 3 new designs that you expect to be better than every layout shown; if you believe one shown layout cannot be improved, say so in "best" and propose fewer or none.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"analysis":[{"layout":"name","strengths":"","faults":"","spatial_logic":""}],"insights":"what the comparison teaches about this table","best":["names of the best layout(s) so far"],"done":false,"designs":[{"widths":[int px],"idea":"what it combines or changes, and why"}]}
